title: Fatima al-Fihri, traditional founder of the Qarawiyyin mosque in Fez
summary: According to tradition, Fatima al-Fihri, from a wealthy family that had moved from Qayrawan in Tunisia to Fez, used her inherited fortune to found the Qarawiyyin mosque there in 859. The mosque later became a centre of teaching. The detailed account of her comes from a text compiled about five centuries after 859.

uncertainty.note: Birth, death and founding years are traditional; the only detailed narrative was compiled roughly five centuries after 859 (src-muslimpost).

where.modern_name: Al-Qarawiyyin (Quaraouiyine) Mosque, Fes medina, Morocco (pin is the mosque she is credited with founding)

importance.justification: Widely credited founder of a mosque that grew into a long-running centre of learning, though the evidence for her life is thin.

sources.title: Al-Qarawiyyin, Fatima al-Fihri and the World's Oldest University Claim

reviewer_note: Least sure of the life dates (800, 880), which one educational page gives without sourcing, and of her historicity: the sources describe the founding narrative as late and traditional. Pinned to the mosque, not a birthplace. Britannica, Archnet and Oxford Reference were blocked or rate-limited, so only two narrative sources were opened.
